status.reasonNotComplete: The helper-owned Windows OLE drop target and its local intake integration are implemented and the native gate is green, but no real human Explorer drag has yet reached the panel. Automated Computer Use pointer drags produced no OLE callbacks and therefore cannot substitute for the required gesture.

scope: Windows Explorer Drop / Node Path-Reopen Preview V0: a helper-owned visible Windows OLE drop panel accepts one CF_HDROP file/folder gesture and passes its selected roots into the existing process-owned local intake basket. Node.js reopens the selected paths, and the existing T-541 persistence contract can create one independently verified child workspace per accepted root under a durable collection index. The browser only opens the separate Windows panel and renders neutral path-free records. This is ordinary local product and 3D reconstruction intake engineering, not browser HTML5 drag-and-drop, retained-handle byte custody, reconstruction, training, cloud or cybersecurity work.

nativeDropTarget.oleApartment: OleInitialize/OleUninitialize on a dedicated STA thread

atomicity.nativeCommand: All CF_HDROP roots are opened and validated as candidates before the helper extends its retained source list.
atomicity.browserBasket: The basket appends no visible root until every returned selection passes the complete batch limits and conflict checks.
atomicity.rejectionQualification: If later basket validation rejects a helper-selected batch, the browser basket remains unchanged and the local controller terminally closes the helper. This record does not claim rollback followed by continued use of the same helper session.

limitations: No real human Explorer drag has yet reached the panel, so T-542B and parent T-542 are not complete.
Computer Use pointer drags did not initiate Explorer OLE and emitted zero native callbacks. This does not diagnose a native helper failure and cannot be treated as end-to-end proof.
Node.js reopens canonical paths after native selection. No retained native source or output handle is claimed to transfer or retain byte custody.

Browser-list atomicity is guaranteed by delaying the append until complete batch validation. A later basket rejection closes the helper; this record does not claim rollback and continued use of the same helper session.
Live browser, durable copy/reopen and zero-process checks remain pending after the real gesture.
SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup is covered by deterministic injected-signal tests; a real isolated Windows console or ConPTY signal-delivery smoke was not run.
Only generated non-venue fixtures are prepared. No user, Grand Hall, Reception, Matterport or XGRIDS source was imported.

A verified local collection would preserve evidence and truth only. It would not approve rights, physical accuracy, reconstruction, training, enhancement, cloud use, signing, publication or deployment.
